subject: Go-live warmup: VPC/on-prem ops swarm + annotated runbook
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@acmehealth.com>, EdgeCloud Integrations <ops@edgecloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Go-live warmup: VPC/on-prem ops swarm + annotated runbook

Hi all,

Final check-in ahead of ACME's scheduled cutover window next Tuesday. Attached is the annotated runbook (RI-runbook-vpc-warmup-annotated-v3.pdf) and a concise smoke checklist (smoke-checklist-20270625.csv). Please review the callouts marked "BLOCKER" and confirm whether your teams can commit to the warmup timeline below:

- Warmup runbook playback (no traffic): Tue 29 Jun, 03:00-04:00 PT
- KV cache priming + small traffic mirror: Tue 29 Jun, 04:00-05:00 PT
- Cutover window (target): Tue 29 Jun, 06:00-08:00 PT

Specific asks:
- @Sarah: confirm Edge NAT / firewall change window from the ACME side and any required special routes from their on-prem fabric.
- @EdgeCloud: please confirm the config diffs attached (net-config-diff-acme-20270625.txt) reflect your planned changes.
- Internal: Karthik/Marissa/Ben — runbook playback leads and smoke owners. Call out any manual gating steps you want moved earlier.

I want a short ops bridge (Slack huddle + phone) 30 minutes before the mirror starts. If anything looks off during the playback we will escalate and consider a short delay.

Thanks — Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Customer Deployments | Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@acmehealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, EdgeCloud Integrations <ops@edgecloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Go-live warmup: VPC/on-prem ops swarm + annotated runbook

Thanks, Irene — we reviewed the runbook. A couple of notes from ACME network ops:

- We have a maintenance window reserved Tue 29 Jun, 02:30-09:00 PT. That aligns with the times you listed.
- Edge NAT translation will be adjusted at 05:30 PT (short window) — this will briefly change source IPs seen by Redwood nodes. Please ensure the health probes tolerate the transient NAT change.
- We saw an expected route preference change: when NAT flips, a fallback path to our DR fabric will prefer a different BGP next-hop for ~30s. We will monitor.

We'll be on the bridge for the warmup and mirror. Ops contact on our side: Daniel Yates (dan.yates@acmehealth.com).

— Sarah
Sarah Bennett
Network Lead, Acme Health Systems
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@acmehealth.com>
Cc: EdgeCloud Integrations <ops@edgecloud.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 13:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Go-live warmup: VPC/on-prem ops swarm + annotated runbook

Quick read-through from the runtime side — items I'll lead during playback:

1) KV cache priming: we'll run a targeted priming job for the most common prefixes for ACME's expected prompt lengths. Expect ~4-6 minutes of steady CPU/GPU initialization per pool.
2) Health probe tolerance: we'll add a temporary probe policy that keeps the instance in-service for 90s of failed checks during the NAT flip window so sessions don't premature-fail.
3) Traffic mirror: request permission for a 2% mirror at 500rps for 15 minutes into the dedicated pool — this is low-risk but will expose any hidden routing issues.

If ACME is ok with the mirror (Sarah), I'll schedule the bridge for 03:30 PT to kick off the priming and then start the mirror at 04:00 PT.

-Karthik
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@acmehealth.com>, EdgeCloud Integrations <ops@edgecloud.com>
Date: Sat, 26 Jun 2027 07:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Go-live warmup: VPC/on-prem ops swarm + annotated runbook

Runbook playback completed this morning (playback only, no traffic). Attaching the filled smoke checklist (smoke-checklist-20270625.csv). Summary: most steps green, two items flagged:

- OBS-PORT-1: Port 8443 was observed filtered on one of the customer-facing firewall nodes during health probe step 4. The net-config-diff shows a recent ACL that may be too restrictive. Recommend ACME re-open for prod traffic or we will risk probe failures during the NAT flip.
- KVC-WARM: KV priming notes added — priming will push a small CPU spike; we recommend starting priming on a single pool first.

Given the port finding, requesting ACME confirm ACL change (re-open 8443 to the Redwood pool 10.12.4.0/24) or we delay the mirror. I'm copying Dan (per Sarah) and EdgeCloud to ensure the ACL is applied and validated.

Marissa
Sr. Operations Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@acmehealth.com>, EdgeCloud Integrations <ops@edgecloud.com>
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2027 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Go-live warmup: VPC/on-prem ops swarm + annotated runbook

Team — after reviewing Marissa's playback notes, we should NOT run the traffic mirror until ACME confirms ACL change. Risk: transient probe failures during NAT flip could trigger automated failover to DR fabric and cause split-brain session routing.

Decision: delay the mirror and the cutover start by 3 hours to allow ACME and EdgeCloud to push the ACL fix and for us to re-run a focused probe validation. New tentative schedule:
- Focused probe validation: Tue 29 Jun, 05:00-05:15 PT
- KV priming (single pool): Tue 29 Jun, 05:15-05:35 PT
- Mirror (conditional): Tue 29 Jun, 05:35-05:55 PT
- Cutover hold: Tue 29 Jun, 07:00-09:00 PT (standby)

I'll host the ops bridge 20 minutes before the focused probe validation. If ACME confirms ACL is applied earlier, we can compress the timeline.

—Michael
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@acmehealth.com>, Daniel Yates <dan.yates@acmehealth.com>, EdgeCloud Integrations <ops@edgecloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Go-live warmup: VPC/on-prem ops swarm + annotated runbook — updated plan

Thanks everyone — appreciate the quick playback and the clear callouts. Sarah / Dan / EdgeCloud: can you confirm once ACL 8443 is re-opened to 10.12.4.0/24 and reply-all with a timestamp? Once we have that confirmation Michael will trigger the focused probe validation, then Karthik will run the single-pool priming. If all looks good we will perform a short 20-minute mirror, then proceed with the scheduled cutover.

Attachments/links: RI-runbook-vpc-warmup-annotated-v3.pdf, smoke-checklist-20270625.csv, net-config-diff-acme-20270625.txt
Bridge: Slack huddle #acme-go-live + dial-in (same as previous invites)
JIRA: INF-3247 (tracking the ACL remediation)

I will post a final go/no-go 15 minutes before the focused probe validation window.

Irene Choi
Director, Customer Deployments | Redwood Inference
